extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent owners, patent practitioners (and patent examiners handling appeals)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for filing and prosecuting a notice of appeal (and related pre-appeal procedures) to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board from an examiner's rejection in a patent application or ex parte reexamination. Covers eligibility, timing, fees, forms, pre-appeal review, interviews, record content, and defective-notice handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may appeal (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant for a patent, any of whose claims has been twice rejected, may appeal from the decision of the primary examiner to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (35 U.S.C. 134; 37 CFR 41.31(a)(1)). Patent owners in ex parte reexamination and certain reexamination scenarios may also appeal (37 CFR 41.31(a)(2)-(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The "twice rejected" limitation need not be limited to the particular application (e.g., a rejection in a parent application and a subsequent rejection in a continuing application suffices). Appeals cannot be filed while prosecution is under an RCE; a notice of appeal cannot be entered with an RCE until the application is under a rejection. Distinguish pre- and post-November 29, 1999 reexamination filing rules for patent owners (different triggering events for appeal). See Ex Parte Lemoine and cited statutes/regulations for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing the notice of appeal (timeliness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal must be filed within the period for reply set in the last Office action (normally three months for applications); it may be filed up to six months from the Office action if an appropriate petition and fee for an extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) is filed either prior to or with the notice of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file the notice of appeal within the reply period, or to file the appropriate extension petition/fee, results in abandonment. Time periods from 37 CFR 1.134, 1.136, and 1.550(c) apply as relevant to applications and reexaminations. Filing an appeal brief without a timely notice may be treated in certain ways (see defective notices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for filing an appeal and associated papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal-related fees are prescribed in 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(6) and implemented in 37 CFR 41.20(b): filing a notice of appeal, filing an appeal brief, requesting an oral hearing, and a forwarding fee to send an appeal to the Board after an examiner's answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of March 19, 2013 the fee for filing an appeal brief in an application or ex parte reexamination was reduced to $0; forwarding fees and other fees are set in 37 CFR 41.20(b). Appeal fees due under 37 CFR 41.20 cannot be paid using the general authorization to a deposit account under 37 CFR 1.25(b). For reinstatement of appeals after prosecution reopens, previously paid fees are generally not required again except differences if fees have increased (see MPEP §1204.01). Refer to current 37 CFR and fee schedule for amounts and forwarding-fee mechanics; see MPEP §1208.01 and §1208.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and signing requirements for notice and related papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The signature requirements of 37 CFR 1.33 and 11.18(a) do not apply to a notice of appeal filed under 37 CFR 41.31; therefore a notice of appeal need not be signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although signature is not required on the notice of appeal, other papers submitted with the notice (e.g., authorizations to charge fees to a deposit account or credit card) must be signed. An unsigned notice containing an unsigned authorization to charge a deposit account will be unacceptable because the notice of appeal fee would be lacking. Applicants may nonetheless sign notices of appeal; doing so is permitted but not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the appeal and presumption of affected claims
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal, when taken, is presumed to be taken from the rejection of all claims under rejection unless cancelled by an amendment filed and entered by the Office (37 CFR 41.31(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant does not cancel claims they do not wish to appeal and also fails to provide argument in the appeal brief directed to those claims, any challenge to that ground of rejection is waived and the Board may affirm those rejections. Waiver of challenges (including nonstatutory double patenting rejections) may have jurisdictional consequences for later judicial review. To avoid unintended waiver, either amend to cancel claims not appealed or present argument addressing rejected claims in the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interplay with amendments filed on or after final action (37 CFR 1.116)
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant files an amendment, a notice of appeal and an appeal brief on the same date after the mailing of a final action, 37 CFR 1.116 applies: such an amendment is not entered as a matter of right and may be admitted only under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An after-final amendment filed with a notice and brief may be admitted if it cancels claims or complies with form requirements, presents rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal, or amends the specification upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons why it was not earlier presented. See MPEP §1.116 discussion for admission standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective notice of appeal (grounds and processing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of appeal is defective if not timely filed within the time period set forth in the last Office action, if the notice-of-appeal fee (37 CFR 41.20(b)(1)) was not timely filed, or if it is not a proper reply (e.g., no claim has been twice rejected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defects are identified and communicated by the Patent Appeal Center (use Form PTOL-461 Communication Re: Appeal). If defects are identified after entry, the examiner should contact the Patent Appeal Center. When an appeal brief is filed without first filing a notice of appeal, the Office treats the brief as both a notice of appeal and an appeal brief; the brief must be filed within the reply period and be accompanied by the appropriate fees. For defects in a notice of appeal that make it unacceptable, the Office will notify the applicant so corrective action (if any allowed) can be taken per applicable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing an appeal prematurely during pendency of a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 or with an RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of appeal filed after a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 and before the Office considers the reply (or filed on the same day as the reply) is defective/premature because the applicant elected to request reconsideration rather than directly appeal from the second non-final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must wait until the examiner considers the reply and issues an Office action; only after a subsequent rejection may the applicant file a proper notice of appeal. Similarly, a notice of appeal cannot be entered in an application with an RCE. If a notice is premature, the Office will process the reply under 1.111 and the applicant may file another notice of appeal after the appropriate Office action issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of separate notice letter and recommended forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of a separate letter containing the notice of appeal is strongly recommended. Form PTO/SB/31 may be used for filing a notice of appeal in applications; Form PTO/AIA/31 may be used for reexaminations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not mandatory, using the recommended form/letter helps ensure compliance with content and filing requirements and avoids defects. When combined submissions (e.g., notice + pre-appeal request + RCE) are filed, rules determine which submission controls (e.g., RCE controls if filed same day). See related MPEP subsections for form usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of filing (receipt and status checking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may check the status of the application and the receipt date of the notice of appeal in Patent Center; the Office does not send a separate acknowledgement letter for mailed notices, but will date-stamp and mail a self-addressed postcard if included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Center provides receipt and status information electronically. For mailed filings, include a self-addressed postcard if a mailed date stamp is desired. See MPEP §503 for correspondence handling guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of appeal after reopening prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: When prosecution is reopened after filing a notice of appeal and prior to a written decision by the Board, appellant must file a new notice of appeal in compliance with 37 CFR 41.31 and a complete new appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37 to reinstate the appeal; previously paid appeal fees generally need not be paid again except as to differences if fees have increased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete new appeal brief must be filed within two months from the date of filing the new notice of appeal (extendible under applicable rules). If a final Board decision has been made on the first appeal, subsequent appeals require payment of all appeal fees. Reopening prosecution under certain Board decision options may or may not require additional fees depending on context (see MPEP §1204.01 examples). If appellant elects to maintain the appeal or requests rehearing after certain Board decisions, additional appeal fees need not be paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Appeal Brief Review Request Pilot Program requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon filing a notice of appeal, an appellant may request a Pre-Appeal Brief Review (pilot) by filing the request with the notice and before filing an appeal brief; the request (excluding the form) may not exceed five total pages and must be accompanied by arguments in a separate paper entitled 'Pre-Appeal Brief Request for Review'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program specifics: Form PTO/AIA/33 may be used; the request must be filed with the notice of appeal and prior to the appeal brief; requests are limited to appealable (not petitionable) matters; an after-final amendment may not accompany the request (any such amendment causes the request to fail content requirements). A request that fails to comply cannot be corrected and refiled because it must be filed on the same date as the notice. If a notice of appeal, pre-appeal request, and an RCE are filed the same day, the RCE controls and the pre-appeal request will not be considered. Upon receipt of a compliant request, a panel (including at least a supervisor and the examiner of record) reviews the arguments, may reopen prosecution, and issues one of four possible decisions: (A) application remains under appeal; (B) prosecution reopened (may include proposed amendment); (C) application allowed on existing claims; (D) request dismissed for non-compliance. No interviews are permitted during the review and the applicant may not attend. Filing the pre-appeal request may extend the time to file an appeal brief until the panel decision is mailed; after a panel decision the appeal-brief deadline is reset (one month from decision or balance of original two-month period, whichever greater) and is extendible under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after notice of appeal (limits and remands)
rubrics_metrics.description: One interview after final rejection is normally permitted (time from mailing of final rejection through filing of the appeal brief). No interviews are permitted from filing a pre-appeal review request through issuance of the pre-appeal decision; except in unusual situations, no interview is permitted after the appeal brief is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews after an examiner’s answer but prior to payment of the forwarding fee are generally not permitted because they may confuse the record, except in unusual circumstances (e.g., appellant wishes to cancel all appealed claims to proceed to allowance or examiner believes some claims are in condition for allowance). After the time specified in 37 CFR 41.35(a), the application is no longer under the examiner's jurisdiction; remand to the examiner requires Director or delegate action under 37 CFR 41.35(c). Requests to interview cases under Board jurisdiction require Technology Center Director approval and a written showing of extraordinary circumstances justifying remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official record on appeal and what constitutes 'Record' and 'Evidence'
rubrics_metrics.description: For appeal purposes, 'Record' means the items listed in the content listing of the Image File Wrapper (or official file) excluding amendments, Evidence, and other documents not entered or indicated as considered by the examiner; 'Evidence' means items that tend to prove/disprove an alleged fact but excludes dictionaries for purposes of this subpart (37 CFR 41.30).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because an examiner's refusal to enter material is a petitionable matter, non-entered documents are excluded from the Record and thus not subject to Board review. Information Disclosure Statements or petitions held in abeyance while the Board has jurisdiction are not entered/considered and thus excluded until entered. The Record includes references listed on an IDS if indicated as considered by the examiner even if not separately scanned. Some physical items not scanned (original drawings, sequence listings) may be referenced via Image File Wrapper content listing entries that point to artifact files; those are part of the Record. Treat dictionaries as permissible aids (not Evidence) during briefing and answering (see next criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of dictionaries and extrinsic aids in appeal briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of appeal, dictionaries are not classified as 'Evidence' and appellants and examiners are permitted to cite dictionaries in briefs and examiner’s answers (37 CFR 41.30 and related discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluding dictionaries from 'Evidence' allows their use in briefs without triggering the restrictions of 37 CFR 41.33(d)(2). This treatment is consistent with precedent (e.g., Phillips v. AWH Corp.) that courts may consult dictionaries to understand ordinary meanings and claim construction so long as the dictionary does not contradict the patent specification. Examiners may likewise refer to dictionaries without automatically creating a new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief filing deadline after notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must file an appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37 and pay the applicable fee within two months from the date of filing the notice of appeal (MPEP §1204 II; see 37 CFR 41.20(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective March 19, 2013 the fee for filing an appeal brief in an application or ex parte reexamination was reduced to $0; for as long as that fee remains $0, briefs will not be held defective for failure to pay this fee or to make any statement about it. The two-month deadline is subject to extension under 37 CFR 1.136. Submission of a pre-appeal review request may extend the deadline until a decision is issued; after the panel decision the time to file a brief is reset as specified in the pilot program rules. Failure to file the brief within the prescribed or extended time may jeopardize the appeal.
